sections.content: The present perfect, haber + past participle, describes past actions that are connected with the present. It is useful for changes that have happened over a period of time and have a result now. Common markers include ya, todavía no, recientemente and en los últimos años.

items.spanish: La tecnología ha cambiado nuestra forma de comunicarnos.
items.english: Technology has changed the way we communicate.
I have updated my device recently.

items.spanish: Muchas personas han cambiado sus hábitos de comunicación.
items.english: Many people have changed their communication habits.

items.spanish: Todavía no he encontrado una solución eficaz.
items.english: I still have not found an effective solution.

sections.content: Use haber + participle when the past action has a present relevance or result.
